main_text.p: longè plura Rabbinorum testimonia Mo-rino in Latinum malè conversa postea observavit Joannes Buxtorfius vir in Ju-dæorum Libris diu multumque volutatus. Ille {t}in dissertatione de Litera-rum Hebraicarum genuina Antiqvitate Morini exercitationes vocat Librum cruda & indigesta materiæ mole infertum & confertum, ubi testimonia autorum Judæorum mutila sæpe adducit; aperit Buxtorfius, quàm multis in locis lapsus fuerit Morinus, quæ inscite & imperitè interpretatus est. In hoc tamen & ipse er-ravit Buxtorfius, dum totus à Rabbino-rum quorundam sententia dependens, contendit pugnaciter contra scriptorum tum veterum tum recentiorum turbam, primas gentis Hebræ[?] literas, in quibus lex antiquitus scripta fuerit, hodiernas esse Hebræas, non verò Samaritanas seu Phœnicias, uti rectè affirmaverat Morinus.
Nomen autem Morini tunc tem-poris in plerisque Europæ partibus ita ce-lebra-
{t} In dissert. Philol. Theol. edit. Basil. in 4. Anno 1645.

page.notes: The text is set in one column with an indented first line on paragraph starts. The first line's opening words are cut off at the top edge of the page, and the first paragraph continues from the previous page. Some letter forms ("Hebræ[?]", the ligatures and the "Mo-rino" join) are not certain; the spacing in the first line blurs the word boundaries between "testimonia" and "Morino". The ligature "æ" in "Hebræ" is uncertain. The running head is set with wide letter spacing as "V I T A" and is given as VITA. Show-through and the blurred right edge are not transcribed.
